questions.q: Which statement about the information security policy and the ISMS (Must requirements of 1.1.1 and 1.2.1) is correct?
options: The information security policy is approved by the organization's management, and the organizational management has commissioned and approved the ISMS.
It is enough if the security staff know the policy. It does not have to be made available to employees in a suitable form.
Only the external certification body needs to review the effectiveness of the ISMS. Management does not need to review it regularly.
The policy must state the consequences of non-conformance. This is a Must requirement.
questions.explain: 1.1.1 Must: "A policy exists, and is approved by the organization's management" and "The policies are made available to employees in a suitable form (e.g., intranet)." "The policy indicates consequences in case of non-conformance" is a Should requirement. 1.2.1 Must: "The organizational management has commissioned and approved the ISMS" and "The effectiveness of the ISMS is regularly reviewed by the management."

questions.q: According to 1.3.2, which protection goal must the classification scheme for information assets cover "at least" (Must requirement)?
options: Integrity
Availability
Confidentiality
Authenticity
questions.explain: 1.3.2 Must: "A consistent scheme for the classification of information assets regarding the protection goal of confidentiality is available." Integrity and availability are a Should requirement: "The protection goals of integrity and availability are taken into consideration."

questions.q: Which statement about the Must requirements for information security risk management in 1.4.1 is correct?
options: It is enough to carry out a risk assessment once a year, before the management review.
Risk assessments are carried out at regular intervals and in response to events, and a responsible person (risk owner) is assigned to each information security risk.
It is enough to report information security risks verbally to a manager. They do not need to be documented.
External auditors are responsible for assessing and handling all information security risks.
questions.explain: 1.4.1 Must: "Risk assessments are carried out both at regular intervals and in response to events." Risks are appropriately assessed (e.g., for probability of occurrence and potential damage) and documented. "A responsible person (risk owner) is assigned to each information security risk. This person is responsible for the assessment and handling of the information security risks."

questions.q: According to 1.6.2, which of the following is an additional requirement for HIGH protection needs?
options: Reported events are processed without undue delay.
Lessons learned are incorporated into continuous improvement.
Handling of events in different categories and priorities is regularly tested.
Maximum response times based on class, category and severity are defined.
questions.explain: 1.6.2 Must: events are processed without undue delay, an adequate reaction is ensured, and lessons learned are incorporated into continuous improvement. High (C, I, A): "Maximum response times based on class, category and severity are defined", plus escalation, reporting obligations and a communication strategy. "Handling of events in different categories and priorities is regularly tested" is a Very high requirement (A).

questions.q: In 2.1.3, which requirement level applies to "Participation in training and awareness measures is documented"?
options: Must
Should
Additional requirement for high protection needs
Additional requirement for very high protection needs
questions.explain: The only Must in 2.1.3 is "Employees are trained and made aware." The training concept, target groups, approval by management, training at regular intervals and in response to events, and documented participation are all Should requirements. According to the Definitions, Should requirements must in principle be implemented. A deviation is allowed only with a valid justification, and the organization must understand its effects and justify it plausibly.

questions.q: According to 3.1.3, how must supporting assets be disposed of when there are high protection needs (confidentiality)?
options: In accordance with one of the relevant standards (e.g., ISO 21964), at least security level 4.
In accordance with ISO 21964, security level 2 is enough.
In accordance with DIN EN 1627, resistance class RC2.
Give them to a recycling company and keep the receipt. No standard is needed.
questions.explain: 3.1.3 Must: "The requirements for the handling of supporting assets (e.g., transport, storage, repair, loss, return, disposal) are determined and fulfilled." High (C): "Disposal of supporting assets is conducted in accordance with one of the relevant standards (e.g. ISO 21964, at least security level 4)." DIN EN 1627 RC2 is a burglar-resistance class for doors and windows. It has nothing to do with disposal.

questions.q: Information has VERY HIGH protection needs (confidentiality). Which set of measures meets the additional requirements of 4.1.2 and 5.1.2?
options: Users log in with a strong password, and information is transferred with at least transport encryption.
Users may log in with a shared account, and transfer through a VPN is enough.
There are no additional requirements for very high protection needs. Meeting the Must requirements is enough.
Users are authenticated with strong authentication (e.g., two-factor authentication) before they access the data, and information is transferred in content-encrypted form.
questions.explain: 4.1.2 Very high (C, I): "Before gaining access to data of very high protection needs, users are authenticated by means of strong authentication (e.g., two-factor authentication)." 5.1.2 High (C): at least transport encryption. Very high (C): "Information is transported or transferred in content-encrypted form."

questions.q: Which statement about supplier relationships and compliance (6.1.1, 7.1.1) is correct?
options: Every supplier must have a TISAX label before you can work with it, whatever the protection needs are.
Information security requirements in customer contracts apply only to your own company. You do not need to pass them on to contractors and partners.
Legal, regulatory, and contractual provisions of relevance to information security are determined at regular intervals.
Once the compliance policies are written, it is enough to file them. They do not need to be communicated to the responsible persons.
questions.explain: 7.1.1 Must: "Legal, regulatory, and contractual provisions of relevance to information security are determined at regular intervals" and "Policies regarding compliance with the provisions are defined, implemented, and communicated to the responsible persons." 6.1.1 Must: contractors and partners are subjected to a security risk assessment, an appropriate level of information security is ensured by contractual agreements, and "where applicable, contractual agreements with clients and customers are passed on to contractors and partners." A third-party audit such as a TISAX label is a Very high requirement that "should be demonstrated". If no audit was conducted, management must make a risk-based decision and keep a record of it.

questions.q: Which statement about 5.2.9, backup and recovery of data and IT services, is correct?
options: The backup and recovery concepts must consider RPO and RTO. This is a Must requirement.
For very high protection needs, (additional) backups are performed via offline procedures, immutable backups or by using an isolated IAM solution.
Geographical redundancy in the backup and recovery concepts is an additional requirement for high protection needs.
The Must requirements ask only for backup concepts for relevant IT systems, not for recovery concepts for IT services.
questions.explain: 5.2.9 Must: "Backup concepts exist for relevant IT systems" (with protection of the backups for C, I and A) and "Recovery concepts exist for relevant IT services." High (A): the backup and recovery concepts consider aspects such as RPO, RTO, resources needed for recovery, avoiding overload and suitable spatial redundancy. Very high: "(Additional) Backups are performed via offline procedures, immutable backups or by using an isolated IAM solution" (I, A), restore procedures are technically tested in a methodical way at regular intervals (I, A), and "Geographical redundancy is considered" (A).

questions.q: Which statement about maturity levels and the calculation of results in ISA 2027 is correct?
options: The target maturity level is 2 (Managed). Points above the target can make up for other controls that are below the target.
The target maturity level is 3 (Established). Controls above the target can make up for controls below the target.
To reach level 4 (Predictable), you must use the KPIs listed in the Examples KPI tab. This tab contains mandatory requirements.

The target maturity level for all control questions is consistently 3 (Established). In the overall result, controls above the target are cut back to the target before averaging, so high and low results do not cancel each other out.
questions.explain: Definitions: "With this VDA ISA version, the target maturity level for all control questions is consistently 3 (Established)." Results: "When calculating the overall result, the results of controls overachieving their target maturity level are cutback and averaged. This ensures that the requirements are comprehensively fulfilled and that there is no compensation of overachieved and underachieved controls." The Examples KPI tab is only for support: "It does not present mandatory requirements for achieving maturity level 4."

questions.q: According to 8.1.3, what is the minimum frequency for regular employee training on the handling of prototypes?
options: At least every three years
At least once a year
Only once, when the employee joins
Only when the customer asks for it
questions.explain: 8.1.3 Must: "Regular (at least annual) training of employees regarding the handling of prototypes." Training is also required at the start of projects, all employees involved in the project must take part, the completed measures are documented, and the prototype protection training concept is part of the general training concept (see 2.1.3).

questions.q: According to 8.2.3, for how long must easily accessible windows, doors and other components resist a break-in with simple tools such as screwdrivers and pliers?
options: At least 3 minutes
At least 1 minute
At least 5 minutes
At least 10 minutes
questions.explain: 8.2.3 Must: "Unauthorized access to objects/ security areas is not possible." "Easily accessible windows, doors, and other components are designed to prevent break-ins using simple tools such as screwdrivers and pliers for a minimum period of three minutes." Reference: DIN EN 1627 / RC2.

questions.q: According to 8.1.6, which of the following is a Must requirement when a subcontractor is commissioned to work with prototypes?
options: Approval by your own project manager is enough.
Approval by the original customer.
A self-assessment by the subcontractor is enough. No approval is needed.
It is enough to inform the original customer afterwards. Prior approval is not needed.
questions.explain: 8.1.6 Must: "Approval by the original customer." Contractually valid non-disclosure agreements exist between contractor and subcontractor (company level) and with all employees and project members. Compliance with the security requirements of the actual customer is ensured (proof is obtained).

questions.q: According to 8.2.5, the access points to security areas must be protected against unauthorized entry. Which of the following is NOT one of the three options listed in the control?
options: Mechanical security locking units with documented key assignment
Electronic access systems with documented authorization assignment
Personal access control with documentation of access and exit times
A "No entry" sign at the door, with employees watching out for visitors themselves
questions.explain: 8.2.5 Must: "At least one of the following three requirements must be met: Mechanical security locking units with documented key assignment, or electronic access systems with documented authorization assignment, or personal access control including documentation with access and exit times." A sign on the door is not one of these options.

questions.q: According to 8.2.6, which of the following meets the Must requirements for monitoring prototype premises for intrusion?
options: Install CCTV cameras and keep the recordings for 30 days.
An employee checks and locks the premises once a day before leaving work.
An intrusion detection system with alarm tracking to a qualified security service or control center, or 24/7 guarding by a qualified security service.
An alarm system is enough. How alarms are handled depends on the situation and does not need to be planned in advance.
questions.explain: 8.2.6 Must: "An intrusion detection system exists with alarm tracking to a qualified security service or control center (e.g. according to DIN 77200, VdS 3138), or 24/7 guarding by a qualified security service." "Alarm plans are available." "Timely alarm processing is ensured." The additional information says: "As a rule, an alarm intervention must take place within a maximum of twenty minutes."

questions.q: Which of the following does NOT meet the requirements of 8.1.10 on image recording and the handling of image material?
options: In areas where prototypes are located, there is a general ban on recording images.
The records of image recordings clearly show who, when, what, where and with what device.
Image material that is no longer required is securely deleted or disposed of.
Prototypes may be photographed with the approval of an internal manager only. Release by the original customer is not needed.
questions.explain: 8.1.10 Must: a general ban on recording images in areas with prototypes; "Release by the original client" for image recordings (directly or by contract); an approval process and clear documentation (who, when, what, where, with what); the original client determines the classification of the image material; secure storage, secure deletion/disposal, and secured transmission to authorized recipients only.

questions.q: In 8.2.3, which requirement level applies to a "solid construction" of the outer skin of a prototype security area (e.g., masonry, concrete)? What must you do if the outer skin is not solid?
options: It is a Should requirement. If the outer skin is not solid, risk-mitigating measures must be in place and there must be evidence of a risk-based decision to keep the non-solid barrier.
It is a Must requirement. Prototypes may never be stored in buildings without a solid construction.
It is a Should requirement. A non-solid construction needs no additional measures.
It is an additional requirement for high protection needs. If the outer skin is not solid, it is enough to install cameras.
questions.explain: 8.2.3 Should: "Solid construction (e.g. masonry, concrete, reinforced concrete, or prestressed concrete). If the outer skin is not solid, risk mitigating measures must be in place and evidence of a risk-based decision to maintain an insubstantial barrier must exist." The Prototype Protection tab has no columns for high or very high protection needs.

questions.q: According to 8.2.7, what is required if prototypes of different customers or projects cannot be segregated on site?
options: Explicit approval by the customer
Approval by your own CISO is enough.
It is enough that all employees have signed an NDA.
It is enough to inform the customer afterwards.
questions.explain: 8.2.7 Must: "There is a spatial separation through personnel, organizational or technical measures", considering customers and/or projects. "Where segregation is not in effect, explicit approval by the customer is required."

questions.q: Which statement about the scope of prototype protection (chapter 8) and the classification of protection needs is correct?
options: The supplier that builds or stores the prototype decides on its protection needs.
All prototype protection requirements apply to every prototype, whatever its classification.

The owner of the intellectual property is the owner of the prototype. The owner's commissioning department classifies the protection need. For prototypes classified as high or very high, the minimum requirements apply.
Prototypes are only complete vehicles. Components and parts are not included.
questions.explain: Chapter 8: "Prototype protection protects physical prototypes which are classified as requiring protection. Prototypes include vehicles, components, and parts. The owner of the intellectual property for the prototype is considered to be the owner of the prototype. The owner's commissioning department is responsible for classifying the protection need of a prototype. For prototypes classified as requiring high or very high protection, the minimum requirements for prototype protection must be applied."

questions.q: According to 8.2.4 and its additional information, which statement about view and sight protection for prototypes is correct?
options: On the ground floor, external blinds alone are enough as sight protection.
Privacy screens must be designed so that they cannot be easily manipulated from outside. External blinds are not enough on the ground floor, but are acceptable on higher floors.
Content shown on monitors and projectors is not covered by sight protection.
Complete vehicles or vehicle superstructures only need to be hidden from view during working hours.
questions.explain: 8.2.4 Must: "Unauthorized viewing of new developments needing high or very high protection is not possible." Should: sight protection through relevant glass surfaces, and no view into security areas through open doors, gates or windows. Additional information: "Privacy screens must be designed in such a way that they cannot be easily manipulated from outside (e.g., external blinds on the ground floor are not sufficient, but are acceptable on higher floors)." For complete vehicles or vehicle superstructures, "visibility must be permanently prevented". Content on monitors, projectors and similar displays must not be visible from outside.

questions.q: Can an organization get a TISAX label by having only the Data Protection module (chapter 9) assessed?
options: Yes, if all 9.x controls are answered with Yes.
Yes, but every control must reach maturity level 3.
No. An isolated assessment of the data protection module cannot lead to a TISAX label. The information security questionnaire must also be assessed.
No. The Prototype Protection module must also be assessed.
questions.explain: Chapter 9: "This tab supplements the Information Security tab on information security with data protection. In order to obtain an effective TISAX assessment of data protection, the information security questionnaire must be also assessed. Therefore, an isolated assessment of the data protection module cannot lead to a TISAX label." The Prototype Protection module is not required for this.

questions.q: According to the ISA Definitions, when must the Data Protection tab be completed in addition, and how are its controls answered?
options: In case of processing within the meaning of Art. 28 GDPR (processing on behalf of a controller). The controls need only yes/no answers.
Whenever the company holds personal data of its employees. The controls are rated with maturity levels 0 to 5.
Only when the company is a controller. The controls are rated with maturity levels 0 to 5.
In case of processing within the meaning of Art. 28 GDPR. The controls are rated with maturity levels 0 to 5.
questions.explain: Definitions: the Data Protection tab "is to be edited additionally in case of processing within the meaning of Art. 28 of the EU General Data Protection Regulation and contains controls requiring merely yes/no answers." Art. 28 processing means that a processor processes personal data on behalf of a controller.

questions.q: According to 9.2.1, which statement about the data protection officer (DPO) is correct?
options: If the company has no site in the EU, it does not need any data protection role at all.
The contact details of the DPO are internal and confidential. They must not be published.
The DPO does not need to report the data protection status to top management.
A DPO is appointed if required by Art. 37 GDPR. The organization determines whether the appointment is voluntary or mandatory; otherwise, a data protection function or comparable role is determined.
questions.explain: 9.2.1 Must: "A data protection officer is appointed, if required by Art. 37 GDPR" (determination of whether the appointment is voluntary or mandatory, otherwise determination of a data protection function or comparable); publication of contact details (e.g., on the Internet); integration into the organization's structure; exercise of the control obligations of Art. 39 (1) (b) GDPR with documentation; documentation of the data protection status and report to top management; sufficient capacities and resources.

questions.q: According to 9.3.1, if the law requires a processor to keep a register of processing activities under Art. 30 (2) GDPR, what should it contain?
options: Full details of all internal processing activities of the company
Only information relating to the order, expressly not other information or details on internal processing
The register does not need to be up to date. It is enough to update it before the assessment.
Only a list of IT systems, without a process description or responsibilities
questions.explain: 9.3.1 Must: "If required by law, a register of processing activities as defined in Article 30 (1) and/or (2) GDPR (in the latter case only information relating to the order, expressly not other information/details on internal processing) exists and is up to date." In addition, the technical and organizational measures required by the information security questionnaire are implemented, and there is a process description with defined responsibilities.

questions.q: According to 9.4.1, which of the following is a requirement for the data protection impact assessment (DPIA)?
options: A DPIA is only the controller's job. The processor does not need to know about it or give any support.
A DPIA is needed only after a data protection incident has happened.
Processing activities that require a DPIA are known, DPIAs are carried out, and responsibilities, tasks and support possibilities in the DPIA are defined and known.
A DPIA must be carried out for every processing activity, whatever the risk.
questions.explain: 9.4.1 Objective: "The handling of high-risk processing is secured in cooperation with the service provider with appropriate measures to identify and, if necessary, reduce risks to the rights and freedoms of the data subjects." Must: "Processing activities that require a data protection impact assessment are known." "Data protection impact assessments are carried out." "Responsibilities/tasks and support possibilities in the context of data protection impact assessments are defined and known."

questions.q: According to 9.5.3, which statement about data transfers to third countries is correct?
options: Transfers to third countries are known and systematically recorded (e.g., in the register of processing activities), and sufficient guarantees under Chapter V GDPR are available.
An NDA with the recipient is enough for a transfer to a third country. No other guarantees are needed.
A Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) is never needed.
There is no need to determine whether the consent of the person responsible (controller) is needed for each transfer to a third country.
questions.explain: 9.5.3 Must: "Transfers to third countries are known and systematically recorded." "Sufficient guarantees (Chapter V GDPR, consideration of decisions of the ECJ on international data transfer, Transfer Impact Assessment in case of relevance, especially in the role of data exporter) are available for data transfers." "It is determined whether the consent of the person responsible is to be obtained for each transfer to third countries."

questions.q: According to 9.6.1, what should an employee of a processor do when a request from a data subject comes in?
options: Delete or provide the data directly as the data subject asks, and inform the controller afterwards.
Ignore it, because the company is not the controller.
Put it aside and handle it at the next quarterly data protection meeting.
Immediately contact the respective person responsible (controller) and coordinate the further procedure with this person.
questions.explain: 9.6.1 Must: "Requests from data subjects are processed in a timely manner." "Procedures are in place to assist the controller in responding to data subject requests." "Employees are trained to the effect that they must immediately contact the respective person responsible in the event of an incoming request from a data subject and coordinate the further procedure with this person."

questions.q: According to 9.6.2, which statement about handling data protection incidents is correct?
options: The processor decides itself whether to inform the controller, and may wait until the investigation is finished.

The incident management requirements of ISA 1.6 can also cover data protection incidents, or there is a separate emergency plan for them. The responsible person must be notified immediately if their order is affected.
Data protection incidents can be handled verbally. The handling activities do not need to be documented.
Data protection incidents have nothing to do with ISA 1.6. A completely separate incident management system is always required.
questions.explain: 9.6.2 Must: "Data protection incidents (e.g. unauthorized access to personal data) are processed in a timely manner." "The requirements from 1.6 of the information security questionnaire also take into account data protection incidents or, alternatively, there is an emergency plan for dealing with data protection incidents." Documented procedures ensure: immediate notification to the respective responsible person, as far as their order is affected; documentation of the incident handling activities; training of employees; support of the controller.

questions.q: Which statement about the personnel requirements in 9.7.1 and 9.7.2 is correct?
options: The confidentiality obligation is valid only during employment. It ends automatically when the employee leaves.
The scope, frequency and content of training are the same for all employees and do not depend on the protection needs of the data.
Employees in critical areas, such as IT administrators, only need the general training for all staff. They do not need specific instruction.
Employees who process personal data are obliged to maintain confidentiality (even after the employment ends) and to comply with applicable data protection laws, and this obligation is documented.
questions.explain: 9.7.1 Must: "Employees whose tasks include the processing of personal data are obliged to maintain confidentiality (even beyond the duration of the employment relationship) and to comply with applicable data protection laws." "The obligation is documented." 9.7.2 Must: employees are trained and sensitized; "Scope, frequency, and content of the training is determined according to the protection needs of the data"; "Employees in critical areas (e.g. IT administrators) are instructed and trained specifically for their work."

questions.q: According to 9.8.1, which procedures and measures must a processor have for the controller's instructions on processing personal data?
options: Received instructions are documented, instructions can be implemented (e.g., procedures for correcting and deleting), and data is separated by client and specific order or project.
Instructions can be received verbally and do not need to be recorded, as long as they are carried out in the end.
Data of all clients can be stored together, as long as there is access control.
The processor can change the scope of processing for its own business needs and is not bound by the instructions.
questions.explain: 9.8.1 Must: "The instructions by the controller regarding the processing of personal data are handled." Procedures and measures are in place to ensure that "Received instructions are documented", "Instructions can be implemented (e.g. procedures for correcting, deleting, ...)" and "Data is separated by client and specific order or project." The objective is to ensure that the processor fulfils the contractually agreed obligations and can detect when the contractually agreed framework would be exceeded.
